# Results — Study 466 (Diamond Top)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **a
diamond top (range broadens then narrows) calls the turn: short the downside break** —
encoded as a mechanical rule. Pivots are confirmed fractals (k = 5, with a 5-bar
confirmation lag); over the 6 most-recent alternating pivots we require a broadening leg
(swing amplitudes rising) then a narrowing leg (amplitudes falling) — a diamond — formed
after an advance; a **short** fires on the first close below the narrowing apex, entered at
the **next close** (one documented lag), and we measure the forward 5/10/20/60-day return of
the short. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce
every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (**total-return**) closes for **SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, GLD** (public, no key) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (**As-of 2026-05-31**, partial June dropped; **21.4** years) |
| SPY fingerprint | `4cb5244f3990` (sha1[:12] of the close column, As-of slice) |
| Entries | **125** mechanical diamond-top downside breaks pooled across the 5 tapes (k = 5, 6 pivots) |
| Timing / costs | confirmed-fractal pivots usable only **+5 bars** later; enter the **next close** (one lag); hold 5/10/20/60 days; **1 bp** one-way × 2 legs per break |

> **Price-only vs total-return.** The ETFs are auto-adjusted (dividends reinvested) —
> labelled total-return everywhere. The Signal axis uses a basket of **surviving** liquid
> ETFs; this is a single-instrument pattern study, not a cross-sectional anomaly, so
> survivorship affects only the drift baseline (which the random-entry control neutralizes).
> The trade is a **short**, so its return is the *negative* of the price move and the random
> baseline shorts random days too — the drift hurts both sides identically.

## The signal — diamond-top short vs a drift-matched random baseline (the honest test)

One-sample *t* against zero is the **misleading** number (it just measures the up-drift
hurting any short); the **Welch break-vs-random** *t* is the test that matters. Δ = break −
random (both are short returns).

| horizon | n | break (short) | win% | one-sample *t* | random (short) | Δ (break−random) | net of cost | Welch *t* | *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 124 | +55.3 bps | 50% | +1.32 | −18.7 bps | **+74.0 bps** | +53.3 bps | +1.71 | 0.089 |
| 10-day | 123 | +20.1 bps | 47% | +0.40 | −25.7 bps | **+45.7 bps** | +18.1 bps | +0.96 | 0.337 |
| 20-day | 123 | −151.4 bps | 33% | −2.13 | −42.9 bps | **−108.5 bps** | −153.4 bps | −1.71 | 0.088 |
| 60-day | 119 | −356.6 bps | 28% | −2.78 | −83.0 bps | **−273.6 bps** | −358.6 bps | −2.55 | 0.011 |

Read it carefully. The diamond top is supposed to **forecast a decline**, so a short should
make money at 20/60 days. It does the **opposite**: the short *loses* −151 bps at 20 days and
−356 bps at 60 days, and it loses **more** than shorting random days (Δ = −108.5 / −273.6
bps; the 60-day Welch *t* = −2.55 is significant *in the wrong direction*). There is a faint
positive bump at the very short 5-day horizon (Δ = +74 bps) — a small post-break overshoot
bounce — but it **never clears the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar** (Welch *t* = +1.71, *p* = 0.089) and
it flips sign by 20 days. The diamond does not call the turn; price keeps drifting up and the
short bleeds.

## Per-ticker (H = 20) — the short loses almost everywhere

| ticker | entries | break (short) | one-sample *t* | random (short) | Δ (break−random) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | 26 | −99.1 bps | −0.52 | −42.9 bps | **−56.2 bps** |
| QQQ | 19 | −515.8 bps | −5.94 | −105.0 bps | **−410.8 bps** |
| IWM | 32 | −237.5 bps | −1.77 | −9.7 bps | **−227.8 bps** |
| DIA | 19 | −15.1 bps | −0.13 | −34.1 bps | **+19.0 bps** |
| GLD | 29 | +60.8 bps | +0.71 | −22.7 bps | **+83.5 bps** |

In the two big equity tech/growth names (QQQ, IWM) the diamond-top short is a *disaster*
(QQQ −516 bps, *t* = −5.94) — exactly because those tapes drift up the hardest and the
"reversal" never comes. Only DIA and GLD show a tiny positive delta. No coherent,
cross-sectional reversal edge — the hallmark of a pattern that re-describes a pause in an
up-trend, not a top.

## Geometry placebo — scramble the diamond, nothing changes

The decisive "does the shape matter?" test: keep the pivot **positions** and the price
**marginal**, but permute which price sits at which pivot, so the broaden-then-narrow diamond
becomes geometric nonsense. If price genuinely respected *the diamond*, the scramble would
collapse the result.

| test | observed break (short) 20d return | placebo *p* | draws |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY shuffled-pivot diamond | −99.1 bps | **0.679** | 500 |

**68% of scrambled-geometry "diamonds" match or beat the real one** (*p* = 0.679). The
broaden-then-narrow shape carries no information — random nonsense diamonds do just as well.
"The diamond forecasts a reversal" is busted.

## Synthetic positive control — the harness CAN bank a real reversal

On a deterministic tape with a *planted* diamond-top reversal (knob `edge`: the downside
break is followed by a real sustained drop), the same short rule behaves exactly as it must —
so the flat/negative real-tape result is a genuine "nothing there", not a dead detector.

| planted edge | n | break (short) | win% | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no reversal) | 27 | +75.2 bps | 44% | +0.82 |
| **0.60** (real planted reversal) | 22 | +1360.6 bps | 77% | **+5.06** |

With no planted reversal the control sits at *t* ≈ 0.8 (no false positive); a real planted
post-break decline lights up at *t* = +5.06 with a 77% win-rate. The detector is live — it
banks a reversal when one is genuinely there, and finds none on the real tape.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The diamond-top short does **not** forecast a decline. Against a
  drift-matched random baseline it is *worse* at the horizons that matter (Δ = −108.5 /
  −273.6 bps at 20 / 60 days; the 60-day Welch *t* = −2.55 is significant *the wrong way*).
  The only positive delta is a tiny 5-day bounce (+74 bps) that never clears *t* = 2 (Welch
  *t* = +1.71, *p* = 0.089) and reverses by 20 days. The pattern marks a *pause* in an
  up-trend, not a top.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is no decline to short; the short loses money outright at
  20/60 days and loses *more* than shorting random days, and costs only deepen the hole.
  Nothing to scale — the only edge (a faint 5-day overshoot bounce) is sub-threshold and
  would be eaten by costs on a 5-day round trip.
- **"Does the diamond shape forecast a reversal?" — BUSTED.** The shuffled-pivot placebo
  leaves the result intact (*p* = 0.679): geometric-nonsense diamonds do as well as the real
  ones, so the specific broaden-then-narrow shape carries no forecasting information. The
  diamond top is a descriptive label for a volatile consolidation, not a turn signal.
